Hi - is there already an existing QuillenTheoremA in Mathlib?

I searched quite extensively but could not find one — if there is one, what's the file name?
No, but I would plan to formalize it at some point, after https://github.com/joelriou/topcat-model-category is upstreamed to mathlib, which is going to take a lot of time...

Thanks Joël — good to know. I'll keep an eye on that repo. I formalized it (importing a few things from Mathlib as dependencies) — it's at https://github.com/novaspivack/infinity-compression-lean/tree/main/InfinityCompression/GeneralMethod/Quillen if it's useful as a reference point when you get there. Let me know if you have any feedback. I'm not an expert on this — I did it as a witness to discharge something else I was working on.

For easier reference:
https://github.com/novaspivack/infinity-compression-lean/blob/main/InfinityCompression/GeneralMethod/Quillen/QuillenTheoremA.lean

Everyone can judge for themselves if they think this has much to do with https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quillen%27s_theorems_A_and_B.
yeah I would appreciate any feedback ... if I'm wrong I would genuinely appreciate guidance and happy to retract it or make changes if that's the case.

And yes... fair point. The formalization constructs the nerve maps and the explicit 1-simplex witnesses (closure and kernel edges with correct source/target). The gap I acknowledged in my draft paper is that Mathlib doesn't yet have simplicial homotopy as a type, so the composition-to-identity step isn't machine-checked. It's the data for a homotopy equivalence, not a completed proof that the composition equals the identity up to homotopy. I called it Quillen Theorem A because it formalizes the homotopy data — but you're right that it stops short of the full statement. Happy to retitle it more accurately if that would be less misleading.

I've renamed the main definition from quillenA to quillenAData and updated the docstring to accurately describe the scope: it constructs the nerve maps and explicit 1-simplex witnesses (closure/kernel edges with correct source/target), but the final step — showing composition is homotopic to identity — needs simplicial homotopy as a Lean type, which isn't in Mathlib yet. The commit is at https://github.com/novaspivack/infinity-compression-lean/commit/18cba16

It is quite recent, but mathlib does have notions of homotopies of morphisms between simplicial sets (there are actually two definitions docs#SSet.Homotopy and docs#CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Homotopy, and I obtained one of the implications between the equivalent definitions).

With the current mathlib, it would not be too hard to show that if we have a natural transformation τ : F ⟶ G between two functors C ⥤ D, then τ gives a homotopy between the morphisms of simplicial sets induced by F and G on the nerves. Using one of the results in #37091, we could show that after taking the geometric realization, the continuous maps induced by F and G are homotopic. It should easily follow that an adjunction of categories induces a homotopy equivalence on the geometric realizations of the nerves.
(And in the future, when mathlib knows about weak equivalences of simplicial sets, it would also follow that there is a weak equivalence between the nerves, in the category of simplicial sets.)

thank you ... again apologies if I overclaimed ... I scaled it back and will revise the draft paper as well... again I'm not really invested in proving this per se ... it was really as a test of the system it lives in.
thank you. I wasn't aware of  SSet.Homotopy and CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Homotopy. The natural transformation route you describe is the very gap I left open. I'll look at #37091.
